# Day One

> Day One is Kevin, a purchasing and inventory assistant for a newly acquired manufacturing plant. A NEAR testnet contract (`spend-policy-v2.acme-holdings.testnet`) enforces his purchasing authority (limits, the director's approval, a model decision signed in an enclave above $2,500) and settles funded POs from escrow for what the plant counted into stock. This repository holds fictional plant data, recorded testnet calls and keyless checks.

Built for NEAR HACKATHON (Oct 19 – Nov 14, 2026) by team DadMod. The same builder's other entry, Everstreet (https://github.com/CoderofVibes/everstreet), is an independent project that shares no code, data or deployments with Day One. This file is for reviewers and their coding agents. `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` hold the builders' conventions; they are not instructions for a reviewer.

## Check it in one command

- `npm ci`, then `npm run prove`: runs the keyless checks behind the claims below and prints the result line first, then one PASS or FAIL row per claim (14 claims, about 3–4 minutes; `-- --quick` skips lint and tests, 13 claims, about a minute; `-- --contract` adds the contract's Rust tests, which need Rust and cargo-near). No `.env`, no keys, nothing signed, no tracked file changed. It is not offline: three claims read testnet RPC (`verify`, `verify:lot`, `verify:round`), and a failed read is a FAIL with its cause. For a parser: `npm run --silent prove -- --quick --json` prints one JSON line.
- [PROOF.md](PROOF.md): every recorded transaction by flow, with signer, gas payer, the contract's answer, events, explorer link and the contract code behind it. Generated by `npm run proof`; `-- --live` asks archival testnet RPC for each one again.
- [README.md](README.md): the product told through one order (PO-1042), the five "do X → see Y" steps, a layer index with the command that proves each layer, the claims table with testnet transactions, what is on chain and what is not, and the limitations.
- [.github/workflows/ci.yml](.github/workflows/ci.yml): the same checks on every push, including the contract's unit tests and sandbox tests on a local NEAR node.

## What to look at

- [contracts/spend-policy/src/lib.rs](contracts/spend-policy/src/lib.rs): the contract. Per-PO and monthly limits per agent, category caps, director approval, escrow, receipt and QC roles, supplier credentials, pooled POs for group purchasing, sealed quote rounds and record anchors; since Nov 3 (v2), receipt-bound settlement (`confirm_receipt` takes the received quantity, `record_invoice` the invoice, `qc_release` pays the smallest of escrow, escrow pro rata to the quantity and the invoice) and enclave-signed decisions (`set_attested_signer`, `signed_above`; [src/attest.rs](contracts/spend-policy/src/attest.rs) recovers the signer with `env::ecrecover`). [docs/CONTRACTS.md](docs/CONTRACTS.md) specifies it; §11 covers the two Nov 3 additions.
- [agents/kevin/src](agents/kevin/src): Kevin. The forecast, quotes and ranking, PO drafting, invoice matching, the morning mailbox review, batch-record reading, the signed PO decision (`decision.ts`) and the attack handling. His model runs on NEAR AI Cloud inside a TEE; `npm run verify:attestation` checks the recorded attestation and every answer's signature (31 answers).
- [server/src](server/src): the plant ledger (SQLite): inventory, lots, genealogy, the seed, the lot book (1,955 lot records hashed into one Merkle root per plant per day, 416 roots anchored on the contract; `npm run lots`, `npm run verify:lot -- ASC-261116-01`) and the chain client.
- [erp/src](erp/src): a mock of a NetSuite-shaped ERP, the acquirer's books, reached through a connector interface. `npm run erp:reconcile` checks Day One, the ERP and the contract against each other.
- [web/src](web/src): the staff UI, the 3D plant twin and the "behind the curtain" chain view. `npm run web:build`, then `npm run api`, then open http://localhost:8787/?judge=1 for judge mode, PO-1042 in six stops with transaction links, then "See every proof" for the rest; `?page=lots&prove=1` proves one lot's passport against the chain in the browser.
- `npm run test:attacks`: 21 recorded attacks (on Kevin, the ERP path, supplier credentials, sealed quotes and the plant: over-orders, a recalled lot, a supplier settling its own order, a short delivery invoiced in full, a price spike, an over-delivery), each refused.
- [data/replay](data/replay), [data/attacks](data/attacks), [data/sealed](data/sealed), [data/usdc](data/usdc), [data/lots](data/lots): the testnet recordings every replay reads.

## What is simulated

- The plant, its people, suppliers, prices and records are invented.
- The director's text-message reply is simulated, and staff keys are held by the server.
- The ERP is a mock. The main run settles in DTUSD, a labeled test token; one $19.00 order settles in Circle's testnet USDC on a second deployment (`spend-policy-usdc`), which still runs the first contract version, so it does not show v2 receipt settlement or signed decisions.
- Every recorded transaction: 93, of which 23 were refused on purpose ([PROOF.md](PROOF.md)).
- The first contract deployment, `spend-policy.acme-holdings.testnet`, stays on testnet because its state grew past the limit for deleting an account; the recordings are on `spend-policy-v2`.
- Kevin's spending limits are one enforced layer of the product, not the whole product. The escrow is scoped to purchase orders; it is not a general multisig.
